newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia signs vehicle deal with Hyundai, Renault.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia signs vehicle deal with Hyundai, Renault.

text.p: Malaysia will roll out its first locally made heavy-duty van next August, to be produced in a joint venture with South Korean and French car makers, company officials said on Friday.

Three Malaysian companies on Friday signed agreements to build a 150 million ringgit ($60 million) plant for commercial vehicle production in a venture with Hyundai Motor Co Ltd and France's Renault SA.
Hyundai and Renault will join Japanese carmakers and France's Automobiles Citroen who have collaborated with local companies to produce vehicles in Malaysia.

The Malaysian partners in the newest venture are Berjaya Group Bhd with a 35 percent stake, a unit of police cooperative Koperasi Polis DiRaja Malaysia (30 percent) and Hyumal Motor Sdn Bhd (five percent). Hyumal is the franchise holder of Hyundai cars in Malaysia.
Hyundai and Renault will each hold a 15 percent stake in the venture.
Company officials said the two-litre van will be a modified version of the Renault Trafic vehicle.
"Maybe the chassis will be Trafic chassis but it will have Malaysian features," Hyumal chairman Tengku Adnan Tengku Mansor told a news conference after the signing ceremony. He did not elaborate.

The second vehicle to be produced by the joint company, Industri Otomotif Komersial (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd (Inokom), will be a light truck based on Hyundai's H100 truck, officials said. They expect the light truck to make its debut in mid-1998.

Malaysia already has a locally-made light van, the 1.3 litre Rusa produced by Perusahaan Otomobil Kedua Sdn Bhd (Perodua), built in collaboration with Japanese partners, Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd and Mitsui & Co Ltd.
Perodua also makes the mini-car Kancil, modelled after the Daihatsu Mira.
Another national car maker, Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton), produces and exports locally-made Proton cars with help from Japan's Mitsubishi Motors Corp.
Proton also collaborated with France' Citroen to produce the sub-compact car, Tiara which was launched early this year.

Inokom aims to initially produce 20,000 commercial vehicles a year with plans to export the vehicles regionally. The plant has the capacity to manufacture up to 40,000 vehicles annually. ($1 = 2.4950 ringgit)
